body.statement: For every nonempty fiber \(\mathfrak F(\mathcal S,L,H,p)\), \( [\underline q(p),\overline q(p)]=[\min_{G\in\mathfrak G_{H,L}(\mathcal S)}\min_{\lambda\in\Lambda_G:P_G(\lambda)=p}q_G(\lambda),\max_{G\in\mathfrak G_{H,L}(\mathcal S)}\max_{\lambda\in\Lambda_G:P_G(\lambda)=p}q_G(\lambda)] \). Both extrema are attained. Every feasible response-weight point reconstructs a semi-Markovian SCM with the displayed independent overlapping pairwise latent parents, and every compatible SCM has a raw canonical response-weight representative with the same \((p,q)\) image.
body.justification: This is the sharp graphical partial-identification kernel: it equates the summary-graph fiber with an evaluable finite polynomial union and certifies endpoint SCMs.
body.gap: DuarteEtAl2024 treats one declared discrete causal model, while FerreiraAssaad2026 gives point identification only on a sufficient graphical regime; neither handles a union of unknown positive-lag refinements with one common micro CDE.
body.consumer: An analyst with a cyclic or confounded summary graph can report the smallest valid interval envelope over every lag placement rather than selecting one unsupported full-time graph.
